title: Service Degradation & SLA Refund Policy
summary: Guidelines for customer SLA breach claims and credit calculations.
policy: Enterprise tier accounts are eligible for up to 20% monthly credit for unscheduled downtime exceeding 30 minutes. Pro tier is eligible for up to 10%. Support agents can authorize credits up to $500 directly; amounts above $500 require human managerial approval in the queue. An incident ticket ID must be referenced in all responses.
action_steps: 1. Verify customer tier and active SLA entitlement via lookup_customer_account.
2. Calculate outage duration and confirm incident ID from Status Dashboard.
3. Draft credit proposal stating SLA terms and credit amount.
4. Submit customer reply to approval queue; do not commit funds without approval.

title: Billing Discrepancies and Invoice Inquiries
summary: Standard operating procedure for handling billing disputes and refund requests.
policy: Review itemized usage before acknowledging billing errors. Refunds up to $250 may be proposed for immediate processing; disputes above $250 require secondary billing review.
action_steps: 1. Retrieve account billing history and invoice identifier.
2. Cross-reference usage metrics against plan allowances.
3. Provide itemized breakdown in customer communication.
4. Propose adjustment or credit via approval queue.

title: Enterprise SSO & SAML Authentication Failures
summary: Troubleshooting SAML 2.0 and OIDC identity federation errors.
policy: Do not request raw user credentials or private keys. Guide customer IT administrators to verify X.509 certificate validity and assertion consumer service (ACS) URL.
action_steps: 1. Verify customer account SSO configuration status.
2. Check gateway error codes (e.g., SAMLResponse decryption failure, clock skew).
3. Provide IdP configuration checklist and test tenant endpoint.
4. Queue customer response with diagnostic instructions.

title: Security Incident and Credential Rotation
summary: Immediate containment procedure for suspected security events.
policy: Never acknowledge a confirmed security breach without CISO and Legal sign-off. Immediately advise customer to revoke and rotate exposed credentials.
action_steps: 1. Identify affected tokens or customer scopes.
2. Direct customer to Security Console for instant revocation.
3. Escalate ticket to internal SecOps incident channel.
4. Propose formal acknowledgement through approval queue.
